topic: Deep Learning: CNNs for Image Recognition & RNNs for Sequence Data

questions.scenario: A smart city traffic monitoring system deploys a CNN on edge devices (Jetson Nano) to detect pedestrians and vehicles from high-resolution video feeds in real-time. The initial architecture uses standard 7x7 convolutional layers with large channel dimensions, leading to high latency (>65ms per frame) and frame drops. The edge engineering team needs to cut parameter counts and FLOPs significantly while maintaining the 7x7 receptive field size and feature representation capacity.
questions.question: Which architectural re-engineering strategy provides the best computational trade-off without reducing the spatial receptive field?
options: A) Replace each 7x7 convolution with three stacked 3x3 depthwise separable convolutions.
B) Increase the stride of the 7x7 convolution from 1 to 4 and append a max-pooling layer.
C) Replace 7x7 convolutions with dilated 1x1 convolutions while doubling channel depth.
D) Apply Global Average Pooling directly to the input frame before applying 7x7 convolutions.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Replace each 7x7 convolution with three stacked 3x3 depthwise separable convolutions.
questions.explanation: Stacking three 3x3 convolutions achieves the exact same effective receptive field (1 + 3*(3-1) = 7) as a single 7x7 convolution, but reduces parameter count from 49 to 27 per channel. Further converting them to depthwise separable convolutions separates spatial filtering from channel mixing, dramatically reducing FLOPs and latency to make real-time edge processing feasible.

questions.scenario: An IoT-based predictive maintenance pipeline processes continuous vibration telemetry sampled at 100 Hz (10,000 timesteps per batch) to forecast heavy machinery failure 24 hours in advance. A standard Vanilla RNN architecture trained using Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) fails completely: gradients either vanish to zero or explode to NaN after 50 timesteps, preventing the network from learning long-term cyclic stress patterns.
questions.question: Which system modification best resolves these gradient stability issues while preserving temporal dependencies across 10,000 timesteps?
options: A) Switch activation functions from Tanh to ReLU in the Vanilla RNN and disable recurrent dropout.
B) Implement an LSTM/GRU network with gradient clipping and truncated BPTT.
C) Increase the learning rate exponentially and apply L2 regularization to recurrent weight matrices.
D) Normalize the time-series using Min-Max scaling and train using standard Mean Squared Error loss.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Implement an LSTM/GRU network with gradient clipping and truncated BPTT.
questions.explanation: LSTM/GRU architectures mitigate the vanishing gradient problem through additive gating mechanisms (the constant error carousel). Gradient clipping explicitly prevents exploding gradients by capping norm thresholds during BPTT, and truncated BPTT bounds the unrolling horizon (e.g., to 100-200 steps), making long sequence training stable and computationally tractable.

questions.scenario: A healthcare AI startup is developing a real-time cardiac abnormality screening system using high-frame-rate Echocardiogram (ECG video) sequences. The training dataset suffers from extreme class imbalance (only 0.5% positive abnormal cases). Fully 3D-CNN models trained on the raw video clips suffer from GPU memory overflow and severe overfitting on the majority healthy class, yielding a high false-negative rate.
questions.question: To optimize GPU memory consumption and significantly improve minority class recall, which approach should be implemented?
options: A) Train a hybrid 2D-CNN-LSTM architecture using Focal Loss and spatio-temporal data augmentation.
B) Apply uniform random oversampling on frame clips and train a deeper 3D-ResNet using Standard Cross-Entropy loss.
C) Flatten temporal video frames into a single high-dimensional 2D image and feed it into a standard pre-trained VGG-16 network.
D) Pass raw frames through a 1D-CNN using Euclidean distance loss against reference normal templates.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) Train a hybrid 2D-CNN-LSTM architecture using Focal Loss and spatio-temporal data augmentation.
questions.explanation: A hybrid 2D-CNN-LSTM decouples spatial feature extraction (2D-CNN per frame) from temporal sequence learning (LSTM across frame embeddings), consuming far less GPU memory than 3D-CNNs. Focal Loss addresses severe class imbalance by dynamically down-weighting easy negative (normal) examples during gradient updates, focusing learning on hard minority cases and driving up recall.
